MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 10, 2020
Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell
at 5:00 p.m., on November 10 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on November 5 , 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Bucknum (teleconferenced in at 6:00 p.m.)
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley (teleconferenced in at 6:00 p.m.)
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Acting Assistant City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting with Mayor Pro Tem Kelley and
Council Member Bucknum absent. The City Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City
Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  November 10 2020
 INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Cox Communications as a Partner in Education

  Mayor Goodell virtually presented the proclamation to Kristen Camuglia, Director of
  Government and Regulatory Affairs at Cox Communications.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Laura Bloom, M.V.: Questioned why Mission Viejo has no regulations regarding Short Term
Rental properties such as “Airbnb” and expressed concerns regarding a home on her street where
there are large parties with teenagers.

Steve Sipe, M.V.: Congratulated Trish Kelley and Brian Goodell on their recent re-election. He
expressed concerns with the City’s sign policy during election season and stated that it was
extremely frustrating that so many of his campaign signs were stolen. He suggested that the City
find a way to have some enforcement mechanism.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: Outlined several concerns with the current Council and their terms, a trash bill
“fake tax,” and not holding public meetings in person.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of October 13, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated October 2, 2020 in the Amount of $428,914.93

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated October 9, 2020 in the Amount of $3,083,887.74

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated October 16, 2020 in the Amount of $722,547.34
City Council Minutes  2  November 10 2020
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated October 23, 2020 in the Amount of $1,041,966.31

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2020

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for September 2020

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for September 2020

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September
  2020

  Received and filed.

10. Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending September 30, 2020

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter ending
  September 30, 2020.

11. Biennial City Commission Member Term Expiration

  (1) Directed the City Clerk to post the Notice of City Commission vacancies, (2) set
  application deadline for January 5, 2021, and (3) scheduled appointment of Commission
  Members for January 12, 2021.

12. Cleaning Services Relative to COVID-19 Pandemic for all City Playgrounds

  (1) Approved the First Amendment to the existing Landscape Maintenance Contract Area #6
  with Nieves Landscape, Inc for the subject services, (2) approved the Second Amendment to
  the existing Landscape Maintenance Contract Area #9 with Landscape West Management
  Services, Inc for the subject services; (3) authorized issuance of a contract change order to
  Nieves Landscape, Inc. in the amount not to exceed $143,680.00; and (4) authorized issuance
  of a contract change order to Landscape West Management Services, Inc. in the amount not
  to exceed $34,300.00.

13. Landscape and Irrigation Supplies-SiteOne Landscape Supply

City Council Minutes  3  November 10 2020
   Approved Change Order to the existing Purchase Order for SiteOne Landscape Supply for the
  subject services in an amount not to exceed $120,000.00.

14. Library Automated System Software and Hardware Support Agreement

  Approved issuance of a purchase order for 1-year in the amount of $73,545.94 for
  maintenance and support of the Library Automated Systems (ALS) Software and Hardware
  Agreement with SirsiDynix, Inc.

15. Contract Amendment for Electrical Related Services for City Facilities

  Approved first amendment for David Electric for electrical related services at city facilities
  for the period of July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021 in an amount not to exceed $57,000.00.

16. Contract Amendment for Plumbing Related Services at City Facilities

  Approved first amendment for Santa Margarita Plumbing for plumbing related services at city
  facilities for the period of July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021 in an amount not to exceed $68,000.00.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

17. Consider the Use of Park Development Fees for the Replacement and Rehabilitation of
  Playgrounds Within City Parks

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Kraig Erickson, M.V.: Asked that La Mancha Park be considered in this rehabilitation
  program as a neighborhood park in need of play equipment.

  Tessa Bond, M.V.: Wrote in support, along with her neighbors, for the Coronado Park
  Renovation and asked the Council to approve a new playground.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to create
  a CIP and designate $75,000 for the design of Coronado Park from park development fees.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

18. Remote Storage Barn - Corp Yard Relocation

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  4  November 10 2020
   Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Goodell, to (1) authorize city
  staff to sign a contract and issue a purchase order in an amount not to exceed $2,000 to K and
  M Contracting Inc./MD BARNMASTER, and (2) authorize staff to proceed with engineering
  and final design.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

19. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Sachs.

20. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Council Member Bucknum.

21. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Kelley.

22. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  No report was given.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

23. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum asked the City Attorney to comment on the history of short-term rentals
and asked staff to comment on what taxes are used on the golf course after her comments. She
congratulated Mayor Pro Tem Kelley and Mayor Goodell on their re-election and stated that the
residents have spoken without hesitation that they are very pleased with the job that the Council is
doing and especially with the Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem leading the way during this COVID
environment. She noted that it was not easy, for all of the candidates, to run for election during
COVID. Council Member Bucknum stated that with less events there is less business and while the
Council Meetings are not being held in person currently, the City is running sufficiently and is
being responsible about social gatherings. Council Member Bucknum also stated that with every
election there are problems with signs being removed and the City will conduct an education
City Council Minutes  5  November 10 2020
 outreach to businesses regarding the sign policy. She shared that under the leadership of the Mayor,
Mayor Pro Tem and amazing staff, the City acted quickly at the beginning of the COVID pandemic
and the $3.5 million surplus is due to good financial management. Council Member Bucknum listed
what has been accomplished under the leadership of the City Council in the last four years as
follows: expenditures were reduced and the Council protected as many services as allowed by the
Governor’s mandates; renovation of 3 parks and Marguerite Aquatics Center, restrooms were added
to Craycraft Park, and Potocki Center for the Arts was opened; preserved 100 acres of open space
with a cash purchase of the Casta del Sol Golf Course; maintained balanced budgets; maintained
strong reserves and increased the contribution to the reserves due to the surplus; AAA bond ratings;
and reduced the unfunded pension liabilities. Council Member Bucknum announced that The Wall
Street Journal named Mission Viejo the best city to live in the State of California and among the
best nation-wide.

City Manager Dennis Wilberg stated that no taxes were used for the golf course and if residents
want more detail, a staff report was presented at the October 13 City Council Meeting. The City
closed out the last fiscal year with reserves at $25.2 million dollars and another $2 million is
expected from the Trumark Development Project which will bring reserves up to $27.2 million by
the end of the year.

City Attorney Bill Curley explained that City staff have been monitoring the legalities of short-term
rentals within the City and he noted that the City has a very low rate of problems. When issues
arise, they are managed by his office and the Code Enforcement division.

Council Member Bucknum expressed support for Council Member Sachs’ recommendation to
work closely with the homeowner associations (HOAs) in regards to fire mitigation and suggested
that perhaps a webinar can be shared with the HOA’s. Lastly, she said she is in support of not
holding a council meeting the week of Thanksgiving.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths pointed out that today is the 245th birthday of the Marine Corps and
tomorrow the nation will be celebrating Veterans Day. He thanked firefighters for their hard work
during the recent fires near Mission Viejo and lastly, he congratulated both Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
and Mayor Goodell on their re-election.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs congratulated Mayor Goodell and Mayor Pro Tem Kelley on their re-
election. He stated that he likes Council Member Bucknum’s suggestion for a webinar on the fire
mitigated areas in the City to be shared with the homeowner associations. He also noted that the
Oso Creek Golf Course is moving along and residents should stay tuned for future announcements.
He reiterated that the golf course is being supported by revenue only, and that no taxes or fees are
being used. Finally, Council Member Sachs encouraged residents to view the City’s virtual
Veterans Day Ceremony.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked all the voters who re-elected her. She stated that she is very humbled
by the support and the confidence the voters have put in her and she will continue to do her very
City Council Minutes  6  November 10 2020
 best for the city that she loves. She wished the Marine Corps a happy birthday and she also thanked
all of the firefighters that fought the recent fires. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that there will
be a blood drive on Monday, November 16 in the Saddleback Room at City Hall. She also shared
that Saddleback Valley Unified School District received a Reader’s Choice Award as the best
school district in Orange County by O.C. Parenting Magazine, and Mission Viejo High School was
also recognized as the best public or charter high school. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that
the virtual Veteran’s Day Ceremony will feature the Commanding Officer of the City’s adopted
Marine battalion, Colonel Folsom, as the keynote speaker. She thanked all veterans including
Council Member Raths and Council Member Sachs for their service. Lastly, she announced the
Character Word for the month of November is thankfulness.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell thanked the voters for their support in his re-election and noted that voter turnout
was at 85%. He announced that the City Council will not hold a meeting the week of Thanksgiving
and will adjourn this meeting to December 8. He thanked all the veterans, first responders and
police personnel for their hard work and asked residents to pray for the two wounded firefighters.
Mayor Goodell mentioned that next week he will be attending a “thank you reception” for first
responders at Mission Hospital. And lastly, due to the rise in COVID-19 cases, Mayor Goodell
asked that residents stay diligent by wearing masks, social distancing and washing their hands.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:16 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session
and by consensus of the City Council, Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, December
8, 2020, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of December 8, 2020

City Council Minutes  7  November 10 2020
